blocks.text: The chapter moves from a vision of four colored chariots coming from between bronze mountains to an enacted instruction involving silver, gold, Joshua the high priest, and crowns kept as a temple memorial. In the vision, the angel identifies the chariots as the four winds or spirits of heaven, sent out from the divine presence and directed through the earth. The later scene records the crowning of Joshua and the proclamation concerning the Branch, without requiring the reader to treat the symbolic vision and the crowning as the same event or image.
